event: Spec says the SHA-disabled code isn't used; the IP reports SwPushMsgWhenDisallowed. So the code is right and the comment is just loosely worded; the finding's premise is wrong.

I withdrew the finding. The test's expectation is correct, so the comment and the check don't actually contradict each other.

The HMAC programmer's guide (`hw/ip/hmac/doc/programmers_guide.md:179`) says `SwPushMsgWhenShaDisabled` (0x1) is not used in the current IP. It says the IP reports `SwPushMsgWhenDisallowed` (0x5) instead, so pushing a message while SHA is disabled should produce 0x5. The check at `sw/device/tests/hmac_error_conditions_test.c:157` expects exactly that. The same "not used" note appears in `hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_sha2_pkg.sv`.

I did not look into whether the plan item (p5.k2) is covered elsewhere.
